$comment: Claude Code settings for the agent session. Deny rules still apply under
--dangerously-skip-permissions; allow rules are what that flag makes moot.
This is a short list on purpose. The design stance is reversibility over
prevention: a wrong edit costs a git revert, so the walls are only for the
things revert cannot undo — a leaked secret is out, a push is published, and a
weakened supervisor makes every later job less trustworthy without anyone
scripts/deploy.sh is EDITABLE (2026-09-09) and running it is still denied.
A feature that compiles into the image is not finished until deploy.sh greps
the image for it, so denying the edit meant no agent could ever land a whole
feature — §14 shipped without its marker for exactly this reason. The edit is
reversible and lands in a diff a human reads; the deploy is the sequencing
rule, and that is the half worth keeping. agent-test.sh stays denied: it is
the gate that decides whether the agent's own work survives.
The last group exists because this runs as the operator on their own Mac, so
Bash can reach the whole home directory. File tools are already confined to
the repo by the working directory; these cover the shell path to the secrets
